page_header: Cell Cycle and Cell Division · 4 marks

steps.label: Why it was called a resting phase
lines: Interphase is the period between two successive
No chromosome movement and no division of the
nucleus or the cytoplasm can be seen in it, and
that is the only reason it was called a resting
It lasts more than 95% of the cell cycle — about
23 hours in a 24 hour human cell cycle.
steps.why: The word 'resting' describes what an early microscopist could not see, not what the cell is doing. Saying that first sets up the rest of the answer, which lists what is actually going on.
common_mistakes: Writing that nothing happens in interphase. That is the belief the question asks you to correct.
Calling interphase a stage of mitosis. It is the phase between two divisions.
steps.memory_tip: Resting means no visible division, not no activity.
steps.margin_note: Open by saying what 'resting' was meant to describe. Two lines.

steps.label: Labelled cell cycle diagram
steps.why: The cycle drawn as a circle shows the point of the answer at a glance: G₁, S and G₂ together fill almost the whole ring, and M phase is the thin slice.
common_mistakes: Drawing the four parts equal in size. M phase must look much smaller than interphase.
Leaving the interphase bracket off. Without it the diagram does not answer the question.
steps.memory_tip: Draw the circle, cut a thin slice for M phase, and bracket the rest as interphase.
steps.margin_note: A labelled circle is enough. Do not draw the stages of mitosis inside it.

steps.label: G₁, S and G₂

lines.text: G₁ phase — the cell is metabolically active
and grows continuously, but DNA is not made.
S phase — DNA is replicated and the amount
doubles from 2C to 4C. In an animal cell the
G₂ phase — proteins are made, the cell keeps
growing, and the material needed for division

steps.why: Each of the three sub-phases has work of its own, so listing them one by one is the direct evidence that interphase is not rest.
common_mistakes: Saying DNA is made in G₁ or G₂. Only S phase makes DNA.
Saying centrioles duplicate in plant cells. Plant cells have no centrioles.
steps.memory_tip: G₁ grow, S copy, G₂ grow again. Two growth phases with the copying in between.
steps.margin_note: One line per sub-phase. This step alone carries a full mark.

steps.label: Conclusion

lines.text: Interphase is a phase of intense preparation, not a phase of rest.

lines: DNA replication, synthesis of histones and other
proteins, production of RNA and ATP, and
duplication of organelles all take place in it. A cell
that did none of this could not divide at all.
steps.why: The last mark is for the direct answer to the word 'comment': name the activities that fill the phase and state the conclusion in one sentence.
common_mistakes: Ending without a conclusion sentence. The question asks you to comment, so say it plainly.
steps.memory_tip: Replication, protein synthesis, RNA, ATP, organelles. Five kinds of work, no rest.
steps.margin_note: One boxed sentence plus the list of activities. That closes the answer.

insider_note: This is a comment question, so the marks sit in the contrast: what 'resting' meant, and what actually happens. The diagram is the fastest mark on the page.
